props.damping: Spring friction. Low lets the head ring past a state and come back, which is charming on a scrubber and disastrous on the fields it drives — this is the control that decides which of those you get.
props.tickDensity: How many states the rail actually draws. All is truthful and unreadable past about sixty entries; even samples at a fixed pitch and leaves the true count in the label instead.
props.showLabels: The action name and position under the rail. Without it a scrub is a position; with it, it is a history you can read while dragging.
props.railHeight: Thickness of the rail, and of every branch beside it. Thin reads as a scrubber under a document; thick reads as the primary control on the screen.
props.accentColor: The trunk, the head, and the travelled portion.
props.branchColor: Abandoned futures. Deliberately a warm off-accent rather than a dimmed trunk — a discarded future is a different kind of thing from a quiet one, not a fainter version of the same thing.

stream.description: An AI response surface that streams the way live chat UIs stream. A shimmer while the model thinks, tokens arriving on an irregular clock and blurring into place, a generation caret riding the last word, and stop and regenerate controls that actually interrupt. The cadence rides the animation clock rather than timer chains, so pausing the bench freezes generation mid-word. Only the trailing window of tokens are live animated elements, and everything older folds into one static text node, so a long answer never accumulates a thousand springs. An invisible ghost of the full answer holds the final height, so neither the thinking-to-streaming swap nor the stream itself ever moves layout.

props.jitter: Cadence irregularity — bursts and occasional stalls that make it read as a live model rather than a metronome.
props.chunking: Emission granularity. Words read like a model; characters read like a terminal.
props.thinkingMs: Shimmer skeleton phase before the first token.
props.caret: Generation caret riding the last token.
props.autoReplay: Regenerate automatically after settling, so the demo loops hands-free.

infinite-canvas.description: A pannable, zoomable infinite board holding real DOM cards. One world element under a single translate-and-scale, so focus survives and nothing ever remounts when the camera moves. Drag the background to pan with inertia. The wheel zooms to the cursor by holding the world point under it fixed, cards drag independently and glide onto the grid on release, and the corner minimap mirrors the extent and jumps the camera where you click. Camera state lives in one ref written by handlers and the loop, and every consumer, from the world transform to the backdrop plane to the minimap, derives from it in a single write pass per frame, so React never renders a camera frame. Arrow keys pan and plus and minus zoom when the board holds focus.

props.friction: Glide decay after a thrown pan — low stops dead, high coasts.
props.minZoom: How far out the camera may pull.
props.maxZoom: How far in the camera may push.
props.gridSnap: Dropped cards glide onto the nearest grid point.
props.gridSize: World-space grid pitch — the snap target and the backdrop's cell size both.
props.minimap: Corner map of the extent; click it to jump the camera.
props.backdrop: The plane texture that moves with the camera — it is what makes the pan legible.

patchbay.description: A modular-synth patch bay. The jacks are real DOM buttons, focusable, labelled and keyboard-patchable, and only the cables live on a canvas underneath the pointer's reach, because a cable is pure paint: a quadratic Bézier whose control point hangs below the midpoint by a sprung sag. Drag from any jack and a live cable follows the hand. Release near a jack on the opposite bank and it seats with an overshoot-and-settle wobble, elsewhere it retracts. Seated cables carry signal pulses on a bounded phase, grabbing an occupied input picks its cable up to repatch, and resizing the bay shakes every cable, which is follow-through, cheaply.

props.droop: Cable slack at rest — how far the middle hangs.
props.wobble: Spring in the sag when a cable seats or the bay resizes.
props.pulseSpeed: Signal travel rate along a connected cable.
props.pulseCount: Pulses in flight per cable; 0 runs the bay dark.

keycast.description: A streamer-style keyboard HUD: every chord you press appears as a row of keycaps and ages away, with a hammered key folding into one cap wearing a ×n badge. The listener is display-only by contract. It never prevents or stops an event, bails inside editable targets and mid-IME composition, and ignores lone modifiers, so the page underneath keeps every shortcut it had and the HUD merely reports what the hands did. Entry timestamps ride the loop clock rather than the wall clock, so pausing the bench freezes the stack mid-fade instead of evicting it all on resume, and a scripted demo reel keeps the pane alive whenever the real keyboard goes quiet.

props.lifetime: How long a chord stays on the HUD before it fades out.
props.maxVisible: History depth; older entries are evicted early.
props.corner: Where the stack anchors in its pane.
props.combineRepeats: Fold a hammered key into one cap with a ×n badge.
props.platform: ⌘⌥⇧⌃ glyphs or Ctrl / Alt / Shift words.
props.demo: Replay a scripted set of chords whenever the keyboard goes quiet.
props.capSize: Keycap height; legends scale with it.
props.accent: Modifier caps and the ring on the newest chord.

file-explorer.description: A persistent three-pane file manager that stores real image, video, and blob uploads 100% client-side — OPFS when available, IndexedDB everywhere else — with nested folders, search, sort, drag-and-drop upload, move, and a live preview panel.

props.defaultView: Initial content layout. The toolbar toggle overrides it live.
props.thumbnailSize: Grid tile edge length. Larger tiles, fewer columns.
props.density: Row height and padding for the list view and folder rail.
props.sortBy: Initial sort field. The toolbar sort menu overrides it live.
props.showDetails: Open the detail panel when a single file is selected.
props.showHidden: Reveal entries whose name starts with a dot.
props.allowUpload: Enable drag-and-drop and the Add button. Off makes the explorer read-only for new files.
props.allowDelete: Enable delete, rename, and move. Off locks the store's contents.
props.undoWindowMs: Grace period to undo a delete. 0 deletes immediately.
props.accent: Selection highlight, active folder, and focus accent.

elastic.description: Throw the top card and the speed you released it at carries into the spring — throw it far enough and it cycles to the back of the deck instead of coming home.

props.stiffness: How strongly the spring pulls home. Higher is snappier.
props.damping: How fast it settles. Lower overshoots and oscillates.
props.mass: How heavy the card feels. More mass is more sluggish.
props.bounds: How far the card may travel from home.
props.rubberBand: Give past the bounds, hard wall → loose.
props.flickPower: Multiplier on the release velocity handed to the spring.
props.cards: How many cards in the stack.
props.throwThreshold: Throw distance past which the card cycles to the back instead of springing home. Capped at 90% of bounds so it stays reachable.

masonry.description: A Pinterest-style grid where every item drops into the shortest column, packed by measurement rather than by a shared row baseline.

props.minColumnWidth: Target column width. The column count is derived from the container, not the viewport.
props.maxColumns: Ceiling on the derived column count, however wide the container gets.
props.gap: Space between columns and between stacked items.
props.packing: Balanced packs into the shortest column; sequential keeps strict left-to-right order.
props.transition: How long an item takes to glide to a new slot. 0 snaps.
props.stagger: Delay added per item as a batch reveals.
props.revealOnScroll: Fade and rise each item in as it enters the viewport.
props.revealDistance: How far an item rises on reveal.

rubiks-cube.description: A Rubik's cube that scrambles and solves itself on an endless loop while spinning like a planet. Two independent rotation layers, and every quarter-turn is quantised back to exact integers, so an hour of turns drifts by nothing at all.

props.autoRotate: Spin the whole cube on its own axis, independently of the solve loop. Off leaves the cube still while it keeps scrambling and solving.
props.rotationSpeed: Multiplier on the ambient spin rate. A drag re-aims the spin axis but never changes this — direction is yours, speed is the component's.
props.moveDuration: How long one quarter-turn takes. The ease overshoots slightly and settles back, which is the mechanical click a real cube makes.
props.scrambleMoveCount: Quarter-turns per scramble. The solve is this sequence replayed backwards and negated, so a longer scramble buys a longer solve for free.
props.pauseBetweenCycles: Beat of stillness between scramble and solve. Zero runs the two together into one continuous churn.
props.cameraDistance: Orbit radius, which is what sets the cube's apparent size. Drag anywhere to orbit; elevation stops short of the poles so the cube never tumbles sideways.
props.gap: Space between cubies, in cubie widths. Widen it and the black core shows through the seams, exactly as a real cube's does.
props.palette: Named sticker scheme. The component also takes a `colors` record to override any individual face.
props.bodyColor: Plastic behind the stickers, and the core seen through the seams.
props.background: The dark field the cube turns in.
props.glossy: Wet-lacquer clearcoat plus a faint oil-slick sheen, lit by a small studio environment. Off leaves flat matte plastic.
props.glow: Emissive stickers plus an additive amethyst halo at the silhouette. Off by default: it is a flourish, not the point.

timeline-scrubber.description: Drag the head, snap it to markers, zoom into the track and let the viewport follow playback. One derived number — pixels per second — places the ticks, the pips, the head, the drag target and the follow scroll, so nothing on screen can disagree about where a time actually is.

props.duration: Total length of the timeline. Everything on screen is a fraction of it, so shortening it zooms the whole track in rather than trimming the right-hand end off.
props.fps: Frames per second. Sets the last field of the timecode and the size of an arrow-key step — one frame, because a finer step would move the head without moving the readout, which reads as the control being broken.
props.zoom: Initial horizontal zoom; Ctrl/Cmd + wheel overrides it live and holds the time under the cursor fixed while it does. 1 fits the whole duration in the viewport, which is the only zoom at which the scrollbar is guaranteed absent.
props.snapThreshold: How close the pointer has to be to a marker to snap onto it. Specified in pixels and converted through the current zoom, because what makes a snap feel right is the distance on screen — a tolerance in seconds is generous zoomed out, unusable zoomed in, and needs re-tuning at every zoom. Hold Alt while dragging to bypass it.
props.showRuler: Show the tick ruler above the lane. Its divisions come off a fixed 1-2-5 ladder rather than being computed, so zooming walks through the same handful of intervals instead of inventing a new one at every step.
props.showMarkers: Show the marker pips. Off also disables snapping — there is nothing to snap to, and leaving invisible snap targets on the track is how a scrubber earns a reputation for fighting you.
props.loop: Wrap to the start on reaching the end. The overshoot carries across the wrap rather than being discarded, so a looping timeline does not run gradually slow at high playback rates.
props.playbackRate: Playback speed. The clock advances by real elapsed time from the runtime host, not by a fixed increment per frame, so a dropped frame costs a frame of smoothness and never a frame of time.
props.follow: What the viewport does when the head runs past its edge while playing. Page jumps a whole viewport and leaves the ruler still most of the time, which is what makes it readable; center pins the head and moves the world instead, which never loses it but never lets the ruler rest.
props.trackHeight: Height of the lane under the ruler. The playhead spans ruler and lane together, so this changes how much of the track the head has to cross rather than how tall the component's chrome is.
props.accent: Playhead, the active transport button, and any marker that does not carry its own colour.

data-grid.description: A virtualised grid over thousands of rows: resizable columns, multi-key sorting, range selection and keyboard navigation. Header and body share one scroller so they can never desync, selection is keyed by row id so it survives a re-sort, and focus stays on the viewport so a recycled row can never take the arrow keys down with it. Give it a parent with a bounded height — like every windowing implementation, in an auto-height parent it quietly stops windowing and renders every row.

props.rowHeight: Height of one row. Fixed rather than measured, and that is the whole performance story — a constant height makes the first visible row a division instead of a search, so scrolling to row 90,000 costs exactly what scrolling to row 3 costs.
props.headerHeight: Height of the header. It shares the body's scroller, so this is also the offset the window calculation has to subtract from `scrollTop` — get it wrong and the rendered slice lags the scroll by exactly one header.
props.overscan: Extra rows rendered above and below the fold. At 0 you can out-scroll the renderer and see white bands at the leading edge; past about fifteen you are paying for rows nobody will reach before they are recycled.
props.minColumnWidth: Floor a column can be dragged to. Without one a column can be collapsed to nothing and then cannot be grabbed again, because the handle it would be grabbed by has no width either.
props.stickyHeader: Pin the header while the body scrolls. It sits inside the same scroller rather than in a second one kept in sync by hand — that synchronisation is never actually synchronous, and the header lagging the body on a fast horizontal flick is its signature.
props.resizableColumns: Allow dragging column edges. The handle is a sibling of the sort button, not a child: nested, every resize would end by firing a click on the header and re-sorting the grid you were only trying to widen.
props.sortable: Allow clicking a header to sort. The cycle has three states — ascending, descending, unsorted — because without the third there is no way back to the order the data arrived in, and for a feed that is most-recent-first one click destroys it permanently.
props.multiSort: Shift-click a second header to sort by it as a tiebreak. The rank is printed beside each arrow: two arrows with no numbers do not say which key is primary, and that is the entire difference between two different orderings.
props.selectionMode: How rows may be selected. Range adds Shift-click for a span and Ctrl/Cmd-click for a toggle, both anchored the same way the keyboard's Shift+Arrow is — one code path, so the two can never disagree about what is selected.
props.zebra: Band alternate rows. Computed from the absolute row index rather than from the position inside the rendered window, which is what stops the stripes from crawling as you scroll.
props.showSkeleton: Render placeholder rows instead of data. They hold the exact row height and column widths the real rows will, so nothing moves when the data lands — a spinner in an empty box only promises a wait, and then rearranges the page at the end of it.
props.accent: Selection wash, the active-row marker down the left edge, and the colour a sorted header takes.

visualizer.description: A live map of a multi-agent system: the orchestrator burns at the centre with a tick ring of its own daily load, agent pools sit on the inner ring with beams sized by their share, and every agent and tool orbits its pool. Sparks ride the beams home, faster where the work is fresher. Hover for a readout, filter to a week, or pick an agent and it glides out of the constellation into a drilldown of its latest runs, blocked work and timing. All geometry is pure and deterministic: labels are placed against collision boxes rather than measured, and orbs shrink until nothing touches. The keyboard walks the ring clockwise, and below 640px it becomes a ranked list.

props.defaultView: What a wide stage opens on. Below 640px the list always wins, because ring 2 has nowhere to put its labels at that width and a constellation without names is decoration.
props.showPeriods: Show the W1–W4 toggle. Picking a week resizes every orb and beam to that week's volume, but the layout keeps its slots, since each orb reserved room for its largest week up front, and so nothing jumps around.
props.maxNodes: How many of the busiest nodes take a seat on ring 2. The pools keep their full totals, so a trimmed ring still reports true shares.
props.ambient: Sparks on the beams, twinkling stars and a breathing sun. It only runs once the entrance has settled, while the widget is on screen and the tab is visible, and never inside a drilldown.
props.sparkSpeed: Multiplier on how fast sparks travel. The base speed is already tied to recency, so a pool that went quiet days ago drifts while a busy one streams.
props.ignition: Play the staggered entrance: the sun blooms, beams draw, then pools, agents and labels follow. It waits until the widget is first on screen and never replays on a week switch.
props.showLegend: Legend and keyboard hint under the stage.
props.showSunLabel: Name the sun. Its size is fitted to the sun's diameter rather than fixed, so a longer name shrinks instead of spilling across the tick ring.
props.sunLabelColor: Colour of the sun's name. The sun is lightest at its centre, so a dark ink reads best.
props.accent: The sun, the beams, the tick rings and the blocked chip.
props.filament: The thin filament beside each beam, the dotted links, focus rings and the flag dot.
props.groupColorA: Pools alternate between this and groupColorB around the inner ring.

pathfinder.description: A pathfinding visualizer on a grid. Watch A*, Dijkstra, breadth-first or greedy search spread through a maze, then draw the path it found. Drag to draw or erase walls, or drag the start and the goal to move them. The path updates while you draw. Left alone, it builds a new maze, solves it and starts over.

props.maze: How new walls are laid out.
props.diagonal: Allow diagonal steps. A diagonal can't cut across a wall's corner.
props.speed: How fast the search spreads.
props.autoplay: Build a maze, solve it and start over while you are not editing.
props.boardColor: The grid. Walls are drawn a shade off it.

kanban.description: A kanban board with drag and drop. Drag a card within a column or over to another one, and the other cards slide out of the way. Work-in-progress columns have a limit. When one is full, the board warns you or keeps the card out. Columns fold down to a narrow rail. With a keyboard, press Space to pick up a card, move it with the arrow keys, and press Space again to drop it.

props.wipLimit: The most cards a work-in-progress column should hold. 0 means no limit.
props.wipMode: What happens past the limit. Warn lets the card in and flags the column. Block keeps it out.
props.stiffness: How hard cards spring into their new places.
props.damping: How fast that spring settles.
props.lift: How much a picked-up card grows.
props.tilt: How far a carried card leans into the drag.
props.collapsible: Let columns fold down to a narrow rail.
props.accentColor: The focus ring, the outline on a lifted card, and the drop slot.

treemap.description: A treemap you can walk into. Every box is a share of the whole, and a box with children is a frame with its children packed inside. Click a frame and it grows to fill the view. The cells that stay on screen slide to their new place, the new ones arrive from where they would have been, and a path at the top takes you back out. Arrow keys move between cells by where they are on screen. With live on, the values wander and the map keeps reflowing.

props.depth: How many levels are drawn below the one you are in. At 1 each division is a single box.
props.live: The values wander and the map is laid out again as they change.
props.speed: How often the live values change.
props.labels: Print a name and a value in every cell that has room.
props.colorBy: What a cell's shade means: which branch it is in, how big it is, or how deep it sits.
props.duration: How long a zoom or a reflow takes. 0 cuts.
props.radius: Corner radius of a cell.
props.accentColor: The strong end of the color ramp.
props.baseColor: The weak end of the ramp, and the ground under the cells.

monolith.description: A monumental slab floating over a reflective grid floor, rendered as a fogged 3D scene you can orbit.

props.slabColor: Base stone color of the slab.
props.rimColor: Fresnel edge light on the slab.
props.sun: Show the sun. Off leaves the sky to the stars.
props.sunColor: Color of the sun and the tint it throws on the slab.
props.spinSpeed: Idle yaw rate while nothing is held.
props.floatAmp: Bob lift-off amplitude — 0.00 rests the slab on the grid.
props.scale: Slab size multiplier — grows up from its hover height; 1 is the minimum.
props.autoSpin: Resume idle rotation when the drag ends.
props.parallax: The view leans toward the pointer, easing back on leave.

shard-orbit.description: A giant crystal monolith turning on its axis in a glitter field, or a halo or helix of instanced shards lit by the pulsing core, drag-orbited beside left-aligned copy, fully GPU-driven.

props.count: Shard count, as discrete steps — each value rebuilds the instance buffer.
props.formation: How the shards are arranged: one giant stone on its axis, a rigid halo around it, or a rising double helix.
props.shardColor: Lit face color of a shard.
props.coreColor: Core glow at the centre — and the light every shard catches.
props.orbitRadius: Orbit radius, and the monolith's size.
props.spread: Halo only: height of the ripple running through the ring.
props.beltSpeed: Base angular speed of the orbiting shards.
props.ringSpeed: Halo only: how fast the ring orbits, as a multiple of the base speed.
props.glow: Core glow brightness — the bloom around the core and its light on the backdrop.
props.autoSpin: Idle camera drift while nothing is held.

grid-horizon.description: A synthwave horizon in one fragment shader. A glowing grid floor, a banded sun, parallax ridges and a pulse rolling out of the vanishing point.

props.scrollSpeed: How fast the floor streams underfoot.
props.enableMouseInteraction: Let the cursor steer the vanishing point.

warp-run.description: A star-streak tunnel rendered as velocity-stretched lines; the pointer steers, dragging banks the ship.

props.density: Streak count, as discrete steps — each value rebuilds the line buffer.
props.accentColor: Fast-streak burn color.
props.speed: Forward throttle.
props.steer: How hard the pointer bends the tunnel.

depth-stage.description: A DOM hero stage where any children become parallax layers in real 3D. Pointer-tracked tilt, spring physics, a following spotlight, depth of field, staggered entrance, zero canvas.

props.accentColor: Accent wash behind the layers.
props.depth: Full-stack parallax travel at the deepest layer.
props.tiltMax: Stage tilt at the pointer extremes.
props.entrance: Stagger the layers up on mount.
props.float: Slow CSS drift on every layer while idle.
props.spotlight: A pointer-following light across the stage.
props.depthOfField: Blur the far layers the way a lens would.

eclipse-flare.description: A total eclipse under liquid-glass copy: a streamered corona, a diamond-ring flare on the breath, god-rays marched through drifting cirrus in one jittered pass.

props.coreColor: The light burning behind the disc.
props.rimColor: Edge light grazing the eclipse rim.
props.backgroundColor: The dark the rays cut through.
props.discSize: Occluder radius, as a fraction of the frame.
props.breathe: How deeply the corona swells and the diamond ring flares.
props.speed: Global clock rate for the breathing.
props.quality: Scatter sample count per pixel — the jitter hides the banding between steps.
props.parallax: The eclipse leans toward the pointer, easing back on leave.

tidal.description: A dusk ocean under flat, left-aligned copy: noise-warped swells with wind ripple, sunlit crests, a sun path and breaking foam, raymarched in one bounded pass.

props.skyColor: Dusk overhead, falling to ember at the horizon.
props.sunColor: Sun disc and its path on the water.
props.choppiness: How sharply the crests peak — 0 is glass.
props.speed: How fast the sea rolls.
props.quality: March step count — more steps resolve finer crests toward the horizon.
props.parallax: The horizon leans toward the pointer, easing back on leave.

liquid-chrome.description: A liquid-chrome form of fused spheres over a black mirror floor: rectangular studio softboxes, one mirror bounce and soft occlusion, sphere-traced in one pass beside left-aligned copy.

props.accentColor: The second softbox — the colored glint in the chrome.
props.blobCount: How many spheres melt into the form.
props.morphSpeed: How fast the form breathes and reflows.
props.smoothness: Blend radius where the blobs fuse — low is lumpy, high is one mass.
props.gloss: Softbox sharpness — below 1 the metal goes to pewter, above 1 the studio lights harden.
props.quality: March step ceiling — the mirror bounce and the floor reflection run at half of it.
props.parallax: The camera sways toward the pointer, easing back on leave.

hanami.description: A painterly 3D cherry-blossom hero: a toon-shaded tree over an unbroken meadow, wind-driven petals drifting across left-anchored copy, orbitable by drag.

props.windSpeed: Branch sway and petal drift speed.
props.fallingPetals: Number of petals drifting through the air. Fades out and disables when bloom is zero.
props.bloomAmount: Canopy fullness, bare branches to full blossom.
props.weather: Bundles ambient light, fog density and a wind multiplier.
props.windDirection: Compass direction the petals drift toward.
props.cameraDistance: Orbit radius — how far the camera sits from the tree.
props.parallax: The camera sways sideways toward the pointer, easing back on leave.
props.parallaxStrength: How far the sway carries, degrees of orbit at the frame edge.

silvergrass.description: A field of silver grass under the moon, beside left-aligned copy. Wind rolls across thousands of blades drawn on the GPU. The grass parts around the pointer, a click sends a ring of wind through it, and a drag turns the view.

props.density: How many blades, in fixed steps. Each step rebuilds the blade buffer.
props.tipColor: Color of the moonlit blade tips.
props.bladeColor: Color of the blades near the ground.
props.glowColor: Light around the pointer and in each ring of wind.
props.skyColor: Night sky, and the fog that hides the far field.
props.windSpeed: How fast the wind rolls across the field.
props.windStrength: How far the blades bend in the wind.
props.partRadius: How wide the grass parts around the pointer. 0 turns it off.
props.gust: A click or tap sends a ring of wind out through the field.
props.moon: Show the moon. Off keeps only its light.
props.motes: Small points of light drifting over the grass.
props.autoSpin: Slow camera drift while nothing is held.

penumbra.description: A cloud of dark shards hangs between a spotlight and a wall, beside left-aligned copy. From most angles its shadow looks like noise. Turn the cloud to its true angle and the shadow spells a word. Let go and it turns back.

props.shardCount: How many shards, in fixed steps. More shards draw a sharper word. Each step rebuilds the cloud.
props.lightColor: Spotlight color, and the pool of light it throws on the wall.
props.shardSize: Shard size. Small shards leave gaps in the letters.
props.scatter: How far the shards spread along the light. More spread looks more random from the side.
props.softness: How soft the shadow's edge is. 0 is a hard edge.
props.haze: Dust in the light beam. 0 hides the beam.
props.drift: How far the shards float while idle. They float along the light, so the word holds.
props.snapBack: Turn back to the true angle after you let go.
props.parallax: The camera leans toward the pointer, easing back on leave.

sky-lanterns.description: A night lake with hundreds of paper lanterns rising off it, beside left-aligned copy. Each lantern is lit from inside, wavers like a flame and has a soft glow, and the water under it holds a broken reflection. Sweep the pointer through a lantern to knock it away. A hit through the middle sends it straight, a graze sends it sideways and spinning, and it swings, slows in the air and can bump the next one. Click the water to let go of a new cluster. Drag to turn the camera around the lake.

props.count: How many lanterns are in the air, in fixed steps. Each step rebuilds them.
props.glowColor: The flame, and the light it throws.
props.skyColor: The sky overhead. The horizon is worked out from it.
props.rise: How fast the lanterns climb. 0 holds them in the air.
props.wind: How far the wind leans the lanterns as they climb.
props.haze: Mist in the air. More mist gives each lantern a bigger glow and hides the far ones.
props.reflection: How strong the reflections on the water are.
props.autoRotate: The camera turns slowly while nothing is held.
props.parallax: The camera leans toward the pointer, easing back on leave.

kusanagi.description: A long sword planted in a foggy field of tall grass, with a wide, heavy title under it and a thin editorial frame on top. Wind rolls through thousands of blades of grass drawn on the GPU, and the fog gets thicker toward the horizon. On load the fog lifts and the camera glides in to the sword. Click or tap to send a cut out from the sword. The grass in its path is cut short, then grows back. The button draws the sword out of the ground and cuts the whole field in a ring. Drag to turn the camera around the sword.

props.distance: How far the camera stands from the sword. Lower is closer.
props.density: How many blades of grass, in fixed steps. Each step rebuilds the blade buffer.
props.grassColor: Color of the grass near the ground.
props.tipColor: Color of the grass tips and seed heads.
props.fogColor: Color of the fog. The sky is worked out from it.
props.wind: How hard the wind blows. 0 leaves the field almost still.
props.grain: Film grain and dark corners over the scene. 0 turns both off.
props.frame: Show the thin rules, the ruler and the crosshairs over the scene.
props.cut: A click or tap sends a cut out from the sword. The grass grows back.
props.autoRotate: The camera turns slowly while nothing is held.
props.parallax: The camera leans toward the pointer, easing back on leave.
props.intro: Play the opening on load: the fog lifts and the camera glides in. Turn it off and on to play it again.

cookbookTerms.fade-in-fade-out: Element appears or disappears by changing opacity.
cookbookTerms.slide-in: Element enters by sliding in from off-screen (left, right, top, or bottom).
cookbookTerms.scale-in: Element grows from smaller to full size as it appears, often paired with a fade.
cookbookTerms.pop-in: Element appears with a slight overshoot, like it bounces into place.
cookbookTerms.reveal: Content is uncovered gradually, often by animating a clip-path or mask.
cookbookTerms.enter-exit: The animation an element plays when it's added to or removed from the screen.
cookbookTerms.keyframes: Defined points in an animation (0%, 50%, 100%) that the browser fills the gaps between.
cookbookTerms.interpolation-tween: Generating all the in-between frames between a start and end value, so motion is continuous.
cookbookTerms.stagger: Animate several items one after another with a small delay between each, creating a cascade.
cookbookTerms.orchestration: Deliberately timing multiple animations so they feel like one coordinated motion.
cookbookTerms.fill-mode: Whether an element keeps its first or last frame's styles before the animation starts or after it ends (e.g. forwards).
cookbookTerms.stepped-animation: An animation that is divided into discrete steps, like a countdown timer.
cookbookTerms.translate: Move an element along the X or Y axis.
cookbookTerms.scale: Make an element bigger or smaller.
cookbookTerms.rotate: Spin an element around a point.
cookbookTerms.skew: Slant an element along the X or Y axis, shearing it out of its rectangular shape.
cookbookTerms.3d-tilt-flip: Rotate in 3D space (rotateX / rotateY) to add depth.
cookbookTerms.perspective: How strong the 3D effect looks — a lower value exaggerates depth, like the viewer is closer.
cookbookTerms.transform-origin: The anchor point a scale or rotation grows or spins from.
cookbookTerms.origin-aware-animation: An element animates out of its trigger, like a popover growing from the button that opened it instead of from its own center which is the default in CSS.
cookbookTerms.crossfade: One element fades out as another fades in, in the same spot.
cookbookTerms.continuity-transition: A change that keeps the user oriented by visually connecting before and after. For example, making the same rectangle bigger and smaller.
cookbookTerms.morph: One shape smoothly turns into another shape, e.g. Dynamic Island.
cookbookTerms.shared-element-transition: An element travels and transforms from one position into another, like a thumbnail expanding into a card.
cookbookTerms.layout-animation: When an element's size or position changes, it animates to the new spot instead of snapping.
cookbookTerms.accordion-collapse: A section smoothly expands and collapses its height to show or hide content.
cookbookTerms.direction-aware-transition: Content slides one way going forward and the opposite way going back, so navigation has a sense of direction.
cookbookTerms.scroll-reveal: Elements fade or slide into place as they enter the viewport.
cookbookTerms.scroll-driven-animation: An animation whose progress is tied directly to scroll position.
cookbookTerms.parallax: Background and foreground move at different speeds while scrolling, creating depth.
cookbookTerms.page-transition: An animation that plays when navigating from one page or route to another.
cookbookTerms.view-transition: The browser morphs between two states or pages, connecting shared elements.
cookbookTerms.hover-effect: Visual change when the cursor moves over an element.
cookbookTerms.press-tap-feedback: A subtle scale-down when an element is clicked, so it feels physical.
cookbookTerms.hold-to-confirm: A progress effect that fills up while the user holds a button.
cookbookTerms.drag: Moving an element by grabbing it, often with momentum when released.
cookbookTerms.drag-to-reorder: Dragging items in a list to rearrange them, while the others shift to make room.
cookbookTerms.swipe-to-dismiss: Dragging an element off-screen to close it, like a drawer or toast.
cookbookTerms.rubber-banding: Resistance and snap-back when you drag past a boundary (the iOS overscroll feel).
cookbookTerms.shake-wiggle: A quick side-to-side jitter signaling an error or rejected input.
cookbookTerms.ripple: A circle expanding from the point of a tap, confirming the press.
cookbookTerms.easing: The rate at which an animation speeds up or slows down.
cookbookTerms.ease-out: Starts fast, ends slow. The default for most UI and anything responding to the user.
cookbookTerms.ease-in: Starts slow, ends fast. Usually avoided; can feel sluggish.
cookbookTerms.ease-in-out: Slow, fast, slow. Good for elements already on screen moving from A to B.
cookbookTerms.linear: Constant speed. Avoid for UI; reserve for spinners or marquees.
cookbookTerms.cubic-bezier: A custom easing curve you define for precise control.
cookbookTerms.asymmetric-easing: A curve that accelerates and decelerates at different rates. Feels more alive than a symmetric one.
cookbookTerms.spring: Motion driven by physics (tension, mass, damping) rather than a set duration.
cookbookTerms.stiffness-tension: How strongly the spring pulls toward its target. Higher feels snappier.
cookbookTerms.damping: How quickly a spring settles. Lower damping means more bounce and oscillation.
cookbookTerms.mass: How heavy the animated element feels. More mass makes it slower and more sluggish.
cookbookTerms.bounce: A spring that overshoots and settles, adding playfulness.
cookbookTerms.perceptual-duration: How long a spring feels finished, even though it keeps micro-settling underneath.
cookbookTerms.momentum: Motion that carries velocity, especially after a drag or interruption.
cookbookTerms.velocity: How fast and in which direction an element is moving. A spring carries it into the next animation when interrupted, so a flicked element keeps its speed.
cookbookTerms.interruptible-animation: An animation that can be smoothly redirected mid-flight instead of finishing first.
cookbookTerms.marquee: Text or content that scrolls continuously in a loop.
cookbookTerms.loop: An animation that repeats, a set number of times or infinitely.
cookbookTerms.alternate-yoyo: A loop that plays forward then reverses each iteration, instead of jumping back to the start.
cookbookTerms.orbit: An element circling around another in a continuous path.
cookbookTerms.pulse: A gentle repeating scale or opacity change to draw attention.
cookbookTerms.float: A gentle, continuous up-and-down drift that makes a static element feel alive and weightless.
cookbookTerms.idle-animation: Subtle motion that plays while an element is just sitting there, waiting to be interacted with.
cookbookTerms.blur: A blur filter used to soften an element or mask tiny imperfections.
cookbookTerms.clip-path: Clipping an element to a shape, used for reveals, masks, and before/after sliders.
cookbookTerms.mask: Hiding or revealing parts of an element using a shape or gradient — like clip-path, but with soft, fadeable edges.
cookbookTerms.before-after-slider: A draggable divider that wipes between two overlaid images to compare them.
cookbookTerms.line-drawing: An SVG path that draws itself in, like an invisible pen tracing it.
cookbookTerms.text-morph: Text that animates character by character when it changes, drawing attention to the new value.
cookbookTerms.skeleton-shimmer: A placeholder with a moving sheen shown while content loads.
cookbookTerms.number-ticker: Digits rolling or counting up to a value.
cookbookTerms.tabular-numbers: Fixed-width digits so numbers don't shift around as they change. Essential for tickers, timers, and counters.
cookbookTerms.typewriter: Text appearing one character at a time, as if being typed.
cookbookTerms.frame-rate-fps: Frames drawn per second. 60fps is the baseline for smooth motion; 120fps on newer displays.
cookbookTerms.jank: Visible stutter when the browser drops frames because it can't keep up with the animation.
cookbookTerms.dropped-frame: A frame the browser missed its deadline to draw, causing a tiny hitch in motion.
cookbookTerms.compositing: Letting the GPU move or fade an element on its own layer without redoing layout or paint.
cookbookTerms.will-change: A CSS hint that an element is about to animate, so the browser can promote it to its own layer ahead of time.
cookbookTerms.layout-thrashing: Animating properties like width, height, top, or left that force the browser to recalculate layout every frame, causing jank.
cookbookTerms.purposeful-animation: Motion should serve a function — orient, give feedback, show relationships — not just decorate.
cookbookTerms.anticipation: A small wind-up in the opposite direction before a move, hinting at what's about to happen.
cookbookTerms.follow-through: Parts of an element keep moving and settle slightly after the main motion stops, adding weight.
cookbookTerms.squash-stretch: Deforming an element as it moves to convey weight, speed, and flexibility.
cookbookTerms.perceived-performance: The right animation makes an interface feel faster, even when it isn't.
cookbookTerms.frequency-of-use: The more often a user sees an animation, the shorter and subtler it should be.
cookbookTerms.spatial-consistency: Animating so an element keeps its identity and position across states, so users never lose track of where things went.
cookbookTerms.hardware-acceleration: Animating transform and opacity lets the GPU keep motion smooth.
cookbookTerms.reduced-motion: Respecting the user's prefers-reduced-motion setting by toning down or removing motion.

react-micro-interactions.title: React Micro-Interaction Components
react-micro-interactions.intro: The small responses that make an interface feel like it answered you. Forty-four components covering hover states, cursor effects, card transforms, dialogs, menus and machined controls. Nobody notices this layer until it is missing. Every one runs off a real pointer event, not a CSS transition alone, so the behaviour holds up under a fast cursor, a slow drag, and a touch screen.

react-background-components.title: React Background Components
react-background-components.intro: Motion for the layer that sits behind everything else. Thirty-seven backgrounds that run at the back of a hero, a section, or a whole page: WebGL shader fields, canvas particle systems, drifting contour maps, and pure-CSS grids. Each one sizes itself to its container instead of the viewport, so it drops into a section as easily as a page. Palette and speed are props, and you can tune them in the browser before you copy anything.

react-power-user-components.title: React Power-User Components
react-power-user-components.intro: Components that carry state and physics instead of decoration. Command palettes, ledgers, orbital systems, ASCII render engines, particle and rigid-body simulations. These are the heaviest pieces in the registry and the ones with real APIs. Most run a simulation loop, several own their own layout, and all of them expect to be wired to your data rather than dropped in as ornament.

react-text-animations.title: React Text Animation Components
react-text-animations.intro: Type that moves for a reason. Twenty-seven components for the moment a headline lands, a number counts, or a word swaps: scramble, split-flap, variable-font proximity, marquee, redaction, neon ignition, frost and shadow effects. Each one animates real text nodes, not an image or a canvas copy, so the words stay selectable, searchable, and readable to a screen reader while they move.

react-landing-page-templates.title: React Landing Page Templates
react-landing-page-templates.intro: Whole landing pages, not fragments. Nine complete pages you can retint from one token dial: a brutalist advisory firm, a darkroom portfolio, an observatory retreat, product launches and more. Each ships its entire directory — sections, shaders, hooks, a scoped stylesheet — and renders full-bleed in its own frame, so what you preview is exactly the page a visitor gets. The shared token set means the Controls panel reads the same on every one of them.

react-hover-effects.title: React Hover Effects
react-hover-effects.intro: Fifty components whose main state change is the pointer arriving. Glows that follow the cursor, cards that tilt toward it, lists that dim every row but one, surfaces that dissolve or shift underneath it. Hover is the cheapest interaction in the browser and the easiest to overdo, so each of these picks one property to move and commits to it instead of animating everything at once.

react-stagger-animation.title: React Stagger Animation
react-stagger-animation.intro: Stagger is the delay you put between siblings so a group arrives as a sequence instead of a block. Thirty-eight components here use it: letters peeling off a word, rows entering a list, cells lighting across a grid, neon tubes striking one at a time, particles seeded out of phase. The interesting number is never the duration. It is the offset between items, and every one of these exposes it as a control you can drag.

react-drag-animations.title: React Drag Animations
react-drag-animations.intro: Forty-one components you move with a finger or a cursor, and that keep moving after you let go. Drag with momentum, rubber-banding at a boundary, reorderable lists, rigid bodies you can fling, cloth you can load until it tears, a knob you can spin through its detents. All of them bind pointer events instead of mouse events and set touch-action on the drag surface. That is the difference between a gesture that works on a phone and one that scrolls the page instead.

react-reveal-animations.title: React Reveal Animations
react-reveal-animations.intro: Content that is uncovered instead of faded in. Twenty-five components animate a mask, a clip-path, or a wipe, so the element is exposed a piece at a time rather than only changing opacity: pixel dissolves, curtain wipes, thawing frost, scroll-triggered entrances. A reveal reads as deliberate where a fade reads as a page still loading. That is why the extra property is worth animating.

react-spring-animation.title: React Spring Animation
react-spring-animation.intro: Motion described by physics instead of a curve. A spring has stiffness, damping and mass rather than a duration, so it settles on its own when something interrupts it and overshoots the way a real object does. Thirty-one components here are spring-driven: magnetic buttons, bouncing dialogs, thrown lists, follow-through on a cursor, a scrubbing history head, a knob settling into its detent. Pull the damping toward zero on any of them and watch where the overshoot stops being charming.

react-blur-effects.title: React Blur Effects
react-blur-effects.intro: Sixteen components that use blur as a material, not a filter. Progressive edge gradients, depth-of-field falloff, frosted panels, a city built permanently out of focus behind wet glass, motion blur on a fast-moving element, focus pulls that sharpen as you approach. Blur is expensive to composite, so each of these keeps the blurred layer off the main paint path or bounds its radius. An unbounded full-page backdrop-filter is the fastest way to drop frames.

react-scroll-animations.title: React Scroll Animations
react-scroll-animations.intro: Twenty-one components whose timeline is the scrollbar. Parallax rails, scroll-triggered entrances, sections that scrub a transform against progress. Scroll-driven animation is the one case where the user controls playback, so it has to look right at any speed and in both directions. Every one of these is driven by position, not by a trigger that fires once.

react-clip-path-mask-effects.title: React Clip-Path & Mask Effects
react-clip-path-mask-effects.intro: Fourteen components that animate the shape of what you can see instead of the element itself. Clip-path wipes, gradient masks, spotlight cutouts, torchlight that reveals a layer beneath. Masking composites on the GPU and never triggers layout, so it is the cheapest way to make something appear from nowhere. It is also the only way to show one layer through another without copying the content.

react-layout-animation.title: React Layout Animation
react-layout-animation.intro: Fifteen components that animate between two layouts, not between two styles. A card that expands into a dialog, a grid that reflows when an item leaves, a panel that resizes without its contents jumping. Layout animation means measuring the before and after positions and interpolating the difference. Done right it keeps the element continuous, so the user follows one object instead of watching one disappear and another appear.

react-3d-tilt-effects.title: React 3D Tilt Effects
react-3d-tilt-effects.intro: Fourteen components that put an element in perspective and rotate it against the pointer. Tilting cards, holofoil surfaces, orbital layouts, depth that reacts to where you are looking. What decides whether this reads as expensive or cheap is the perspective distance, not the rotation angle. Too near and a small tilt distorts violently. Too far and the whole effect flattens into a slide.

framer-motion-components.title: Framer Motion Components for React
framer-motion-components.intro: Fifty-five components built on Motion, the animation library that used to be published as Framer Motion. It ships as the motion package now, and these lean on what it does best: layout animation, gesture handling, and springs that survive an interruption. Every one installs with a single dependency beyond React, and the source is plain idiomatic Motion, so it reads like code you would have written instead of a wrapper you have to learn.

react-webgl-backgrounds.title: React WebGL Backgrounds
react-webgl-backgrounds.intro: Forty-five components that render on the GPU through a WebGL context: fragment-shader gradients, particle fields, fluid simulations, an agent-based slime mould, rain running down a pane of glass, a raymarched black hole. Thirty-nine use ogl, a wrapper small enough that the whole bundle costs less than one hero image. Six use Three.js, where the scene really does need a scene graph. All of them size to their container and halt the render loop when the tab is hidden.
